methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $140M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Panthalassa, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Garth Sheldon-Coulson and Brian Moffat, has raised $140M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a competitive set spanning one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers, with primary comparables including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy—all Series C stage companies in the same sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to later-stage advancement against the $140M total raised proxy, implying $266M. Peer-median analysis uses three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.0B, though the range spans $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals), reflecting material dispersion in the peer set. This yields a $1.0B implied valuation.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $226M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $633M. The wide range reflects two distinct forces: the stage-progression method anchors conservatively to capital deployed, while peer-median reflects significantly higher valuations at adjacent stages. Key uncertainties include whether Panthalassa's specific technology trajectory and market timing justify peer valuations skewed upward by two outliers (KoBold at $3.0B), and the relevance of Series C comparables to a Series B stage company.
